TTFT prober freshness (seconds since last push)
panels.description: If this is red, the TTFT panel to the left is showing a frozen number from a dead prober, not a live measurement. Pushgateway serves the last value it was ever given forever, so a stopped ttft-prober CronJob looks identical to a healthy one unless this is checked separately. Backed by the same push_time_seconds meta-metric as the TTFTProberStale alert in recording-rules.yaml.

panels.title: Are we about to saturate? requests waiting and running

options.content:
**Prefix cache hit rate** and **KV cache utilisation** are vLLM metrics and arrive in phase 2. llama.cpp does not emit the KV cache events these depend on. See `docs/adr/0006-metric-normalisation.md`. This panel is deliberately text: an empty graph is indistinguishable from a broken one.

The TTFT panel above is not this engine's own signal either: it comes from a client-side prober CronJob (`platform/30-observability/ttft-prober-cronjob.yaml`), because llama.cpp exposes no latency histogram of any kind. It is labelled in its own title for the same reason - a synthetic number must never look like a served one. Its freshness stat panel exists because a dead prober would otherwise look identical to a working one.

The **context high-watermark** panel below is the nearest substitute this engine allows for KV cache utilisation. It is not the same thing: it reports the largest context seen, not how full the cache is now, and it never falls. Read it as "how close has real traffic come to the context limit", not as headroom.

Whole-request p95 at the gateway (to the LAST token, not the first)
